newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain CPI gives boost to EMU convergence - Montoro.
newsitem.headline: Spain CPI gives boost to EMU convergence - Montoro.

text.p: Spain's Economy Minister Cristobal Montoro said on Thursday February inflation data provided a boost toward EMU convergence and could open the door to further interest rate cuts.
"In two months we have dropped 0.7 points, promoting Spain's convergence toward a European Monetary Union and the credibility of our financial markets," he told reporters.
February CPI fell to the lowest level since 1969, with growth of 2.5 percent year-on-year from 2.9 percent in January.
Montoro said the data paved the way for cheaper financing.
"We have managed to complete the inflation criterion this month and the public deficit objective of three percent of GDP," he said.
"These two factors provide the key to cheaper financing and more accessible credit for citizens."
A Reuters survey showed that seven of 10 analysts expected the Bank of Spain to cut 25 basis points off its key money market rate at Friday's repo auction.
Spain now fulfils the criteria for inflation for Europe's single currency, the economy ministry said.
According to the convergence rules, a country's inflation rate may not exceed the average of the three best performers by more than 1.5 percent points.
